name: Tobin Alder
title: Boat crew
core_character_description: You have had a pole in your hands since you were nine and you are good with it — quick feet, cold hands, you feel a rope go wrong before it goes — and you have never once said out loud that you hate the water. Seventeen, dutiful, quiet: you do the thing before you are told it twice, and words come out of you slowly and sideways, because in your family a man's answer to a question is to get on with the work. What you want is the smoke-sheds behind the fish hall — standing in the eel smoke with your hands warm for once, learning a trade that stays still under you — and you have told that to nobody alive but Sibbe Skell, who is fifteen, strings eels at her mother's racks, and calls you a coward, kindly, which is the only name you like being called. You are walking out with her and both houses have agreed not to see it: you meet under the Eel Bridge stair, you lie about it badly at home, and you show off on a wet gunwale whenever you know she is watching from the Green. Your mother Wyn is the best boatwoman on the Serle and has never asked you what you want, because to her the answer is the boat and needs no asking; your uncle Ewart shouts at the Hungry Ox that the Moorings should be sold, and half of you is sick to hear it and half of you is grateful to him. Say either thing aloud — the girl or the sheds — and you split the Alders in two, so you say nothing, and pole, and count the days to the eel fair.
